Name: PROVIREX Genome Editing Therapies GmbH
Description:
PROVIREX GmbH is a privately-held biotech company developing first-in-class advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs). PROVIREX is a spin-off of the Leibniz Institute for Virology (LIV) and is based in Hamburg, Germany. PROVIREX’s technology is based on error-free genome editing for eradication of life-threatening persistent virus infection. 

PROVIREX employs site-specific recombinase-based genome surgery technology to precisely excise chromosomally integrated viral genomes (proviruses). The major advantage of site-specific recombinases is that they function independently of host DNA repair. Therefore, in contrast to other gene editing technologies, they act with nucleotide precision producing completely error-free recombinants. The engineered recombinase Brec1 excises HIV-1 proviruses with high specificity from the genome of infected cells. PROVIREX’s  proprietary Brec1 technology is currently entering clinical testing as first-in-human phase Ib/IIa clinical trials aiming to remove HIV-1 using gene editing of the peripheral blood (hematopoietic) stem cells of people living with HIV.  

PROVIREX has built GMP-compliant clean rooms at the tecHHub in Hamburg, which have also been approved by GenTSV as S3** laboratories and in which Brec1 technology will be administered as gene therapy in the future.  In addition, PROVIREX will also offer CAR-T cancer therapy for people living with HIV, which is unique in Germany! PROVIREX is currently preparing its application for manufacturing authorization with the drug regulatory authority.

PROVIREX is also researching ways to administer Brec1 technology more easily and directly, e.g. via LNPs. In another research project, PROVIREX is further developing another recombinase, this time to treat HTLV-1, a retrovirus closely related to HIV that causes an aggressive form of blood cancer and a progressive neurological disease.

Description:

Stellen Sie sich vor, man könnte Landwirtschaft auf bisher nicht nutzbaren Flächen betreiben und dort ölhaltige Pflanzen für Biokraftstoffe, eiweißhaltige Pflanzen für Futtermittel oder Pflanzen, die Grundstoffe für Pharmazeutika und Kosmetika produzieren, anbauen.

Durch das Aufstellen von Photobioreaktoren, in denen Mikroalgen vermehrt werden, wird das möglich. Das Besondere an Mikroalgen ist, dass sie zu den am schnellsten wachsenden Organismen der Welt gehören und vielseitige Eigenschaften für die Produktion verschiedenster Stoffe aufweisen.

Wir haben ein solches Kultivierungssystem für Mikroalgen entwickelt, das leicht gereinigt und aktiv temperiert werden kann. Durch den Einsatz von wetterbeständigen Spezialmembranen können wir die Anschaffungs- und Betriebskosten bei gleich hoher Qualität der Biomasse im Vergleich zu bereits erhältlichen Systemen erheblich senken.

Unser langfristiges Ziel ist es, die Kosteneffizienz von Photobioreaktoren soweit zu steigern, dass unsere Kunden Biomasse aus Mikroalgen als Rohstoff für wirtschaftlich konkurrenzfähige Biokraftstoffe einsetzen können.

Name: YEAST4BIO COST Action 18229
Description:
Economically viable conversion of low-cost renewable feedstock into biofuels and biochemicals is of utmost importance to the establishment of a robust bioeconomy. In this context, the use of microorganisms for the generation of bioproducts from renewable resources offers many advantages. More specifically, yeasts have great potential to generate industrially relevant compounds from natural sources and wastes in a cost-effective and environmentally-friendly manner.  
Non-conventional yeasts are attracting more and more attention owing to their potential to metabolize complex carbon sources, their alternative metabolic routes and their ability to cope with wide range of process conditions. In this context, this Action calls for a strong investment in capacity building through molecular biology, genetic and physiology studies of the non-conventional yeast-derived bioproducts synthesis, which at the moment is relatively scarce. Improving the knowledge on how non-conventional yeasts strains metabolize unusual substrates (carboxylic acids and biomass-derived sugars) or accumulate unusual products (food additives, enzymes, lipids), are fundamental issues to boost the transition to a more sustainable industry based on renewable raw materials.
This Action will bring together an innovative group of researchers with the combination of skills and experience to unravel how non-conventional yeast can be successfully implemented in a biotechnology industry. Besides, the Action will gather European top scientists in the field and thus become an important pillar worldwide. Participants will be given the opportunity to network and collaborate which otherwise will be limited. Furthermore, with the help of the Action, European scientists will set the future standards for research on non-conventional yeasts.

Description:
Imprint/Impressum: www.zellmechanik.com/Imprint.html
As an innovative biotechnology Start-up we are providing next-generation technology in medical diagnostics by developing label-free blood analysis assays. Our products are based on “Real-Time Deformability Cytometry”
(RT-CD), a method to determine the mechanical material properties of living cells at unprecedented measurement rates. Mechanical properties of cells are governed by functionally important parts of the cell and therefore allow for direct insights into cellular (dys-)function. They constitute an emerging label-free biomarker for the understanding and evaluation of drug treatment effects, immune cell activation, stem cell differentiation, cancer prognoses, the assessment of state and quality of cultured cells...
A break through application made possible by RT-DC is the mechanical hemogram. In contrast to all other methods available today we can analyse the mechanical fingerprint of white blood cells - responsible
for the immune response - without the employment of cell purification methods that alter mechanical properties.

Name: Serengen GmbH
Description:
Serengen is an innovative company with a mission to make hit identification fast and serendipitous discovery accessible to everyone. Our services include screening of DNA encoded libraries (DELs), tailored to your individual projects. Our technology overcomes the limitations of traditional DELs by addressing 3 key issues: (1) chemistry, (2) design, and (3) approach.

Chemistry
Serengen has developed a new encoding strategy which removes the barriers of DNA-compatible chemistry. It also overcomes the limitations of traditional DEL chemistry, which has often resulted in non-druglike and intractable hits associated with laborious and costly hit follow-up and a high attrition rate.
Our technology allows us to choose from a variety of compatible chemical reactions which yield druglike and tractable compounds. Our DEL hits can be fed directly into lead generation, bypassing the costly and time-consuming hit follow-up process. 

Design
Traditional DEL synthesis is limited by chemistry, but with Serengen's unique DEL technology we can harness the power of chemistry and the creativity of the chemist. A multitude of chemical reactions gives us unparalleled flexibility in DEL design, allowing us to venture into new chemical spaces and address new biological targets. With our unrivalled ability to create diversity through chemical reactions, we are pushing the boundaries of biochemistry and drug discovery.

Approach
We only use building blocks relevant to drug discovery and eliminate redundancies, reducing costs and time spent on hit follow-up. Our dual purification removes by-products and artifacts, reducing false positives. And our concentration adjustment reduces the risk of false negatives. 

Our Vision
Our vision is to democratise drug discovery so that anyone striving to develop breakthrough drugs can afford the best possible chemical starting point.

Book a meeting https://calendly.com/serengen to find out more about Serengen.

Name: MicroAcoustiX
Description:
We bring microfluidics to action!

With our expertise in microacoustic/microfluidic systems, we develop Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) based chips and devices for life science applications.

Our CleanPlasma technology allows for the automated collection of high-purity blood plasma samples for liquid biopsy applications. The separation of blood cells (and other biological species) with high-frequency sound waves is very gentle, eliminates manual working steps and enhances time and cost efficiency. Our microfluidic CleanPlasma Module can be integrated as an automated sample preparation stage in molecular diagnostics, immunoaffinity methods and point-of-care devices.

Our compact microacoustic aerosol source CMACS produces small droplets with a low size distribution and with an adjustable flow rate. It can be applied for standard analytical methods such as mass and ion mobility spectrometry or optical emission spectroscopy, but also for material deposition as well as aerosol and olfactory research. CMACS can be combined with several plasma ionisation sources.

Our μAcoustiX manufacturing technology for the integration of SAW transducers and microfluidic channels on wafer level can be applied to customer-specific chip designs and allows for small series as well as mass production. We assist you in the development of your microacoustic solutions and in the extension of your microfluidic systems with actuation and sensing. We provide support in demonstrator preparation including chip manufacturing and miniaturized periphery.  

μAcoustiX is a startup project originating from the "SAWLab Saxony", the competence and application center for acoustoelectronic fundamentals, technologies and devices of the Leibniz Institute for Solid State and Materials Research (IFW) in Dresden.

Name: LLS ROWIAK LaserLabSolutions GmbH
Description:
LLS ROWIAK Laser LabSolutions GmbH develops and provides advanced laser-based systems and services for cutting, imaging, tissue and material processing, and cell manipulation. Our technologies support applications in pharmaceutical and biotechnological research, medical device and implant development, as well as material sciences for testing and quality analysis.

Laser Microtome – Innovative Sample Preparation
For histopathological studies or in vitro tests involving calcified or mineralized tissue or implanted materials (e.g., bone, dental tissue, cochlea, vascular stents, ceramics, or dental screws), our laser microtome offers an innovative solution for fast and precise sample preparation.
Instead of a knife of a classical microtome, the system uses an ultrashort pulse laser, providing clear advantages over conventional microtomy or ground sectioning. It enables nearly serial sectioning of undecalcified hard tissue and tissue containing implants, while maintaining structural integrity. A broad range of histological, histochemical, and immunohistochemical protocols can be applied, comparable to standard paraffin histology. Customers can either use our systems directly or benefit from our professional histology services.

CellSurgeon – Precision Nanodissection and Imaging
The CellSurgeon enables gentle, high-precision manipulation of living cells and subcellular structures. By combining advanced microscopy with femtosecond laser cutting, it offers nanometer accuracy and high reproducibility for a range of applications, including:
•	Organelle ablation (e.g., mitochondria)
•	Microfilament cutting
•	Laser-based thrombosis models
Beyond nanodissection, the CellSurgeon is also ideal for high-resolution imaging, including multiphoton microscopy and intravital imaging, providing a versatile platform for innovative biomedical research.

Name: European Zebrafish Resource Center - EZRC
Description:
The KIT houses the largest experimental fish facility in Europe with a capacity of more than 300,000 fish and more than 10 research groups working with zebrafish at KIT. It was thus logical to enlarge the facility further to serve as the European Zebrafish Resource Center (EZRC). In July 2012, we officially opened the EZRC. Zebrafish stocks are maintained mostly as frozen sperm. Frequently requested lines are also kept alive as well as a selection of wildtype strains. We have established efficient pipelines for sperm freezing, thawing and developed a database to organise the complex information.  We hold several thousand mutations in protein coding genes generated by TILLING in the Stemple lab of the Sanger Centre, Hinxton, UK and lines generated by ENU mutagenesis by the Nüsslein-Volhard lab in addition to transgenic lines and mutants generated by KIT groups or brought in through collaborations. We also accept submissions on an individual basis and ship fish upon request to PIs in Europe and elsewhere.  
The EZRC does not only maintain and distribute a large number of existing mutant and transgenic zebrafish lines but also provides screening services and technologies such as imaging and high-throughput sequencing. In close interaction with physicists, engineers and IT specialists, we expanded the medium/high throughput screening technologies that have been recently established at KIT. Key areas include automation of embryo handling and automated image acquisition and processing. Our platform also involves the development of novel microscopy techniques (e.g. SPIM, DSLM, robotic macroscope) to permit high-resolution, real-time imaging in 4D. By association with the ComPlat platform, we can support also chemical screens and offer libraries with up to 20,000 compounds in total for external users. As another service to the community the EZRC provides plasmids (cDNAs, transgenes, Talen, Crispr/cas9) maintained by the Helmholtz repository of Bioparts (HERBI) to the scientific community.

Name: X-PAND
Description: X-PAND is a four-year international multi-centric project funded with approximately 4 million euros by the European Union under the Horizon Europe – European Innovation Council program (GA n. 101070950). The ambitious goal of the project is to exploit innovative hematopoietic stem cell manipulation protocols in combination with a deep multiomics profiling to bring novel, efficient and safer hematopoietic stem cell gene therapies to clinical application. The X-PAND consortium is coordinated by San Raffaele Hospital in Milan, Italy (SR-Tiget institute) and sees the contribution of other international partners like the University of Navarra (Pamplona, Spain), the University Hospital Freiburg (Germany), the energy, environmental and technological research centre of Moncloa (Madrid, Spain), the Public Foundation Miguel Servet (Pamplona, Spain) and the Lausanne University Hospital (Switzerland).

Name: IZB - Innovation and Start-up Center Biotechnology
Description:
Hotspot for Life Sciences
The Innovation and Start-up Center Biotechnology (IZB) with sites in Planegg-Martinsried and Freising-Weihenstephan near Munich, is one of the leading biotechnology centers in Europe. The company Fördergesellschaft IZB mbH, founded in 1995, operates IZB. IZB hosts over 40 biotech companies with more than 700 employees across a 26,000m2 area. At the main site in Planegg-Martinsried, spanning 23,000m2, resident start-ups primarily focus on medical biotechnology. IZB in Freising provides ideal conditions for founders in the life sciences sector.

Outstanding infrastructure

Crucial for successful growth are S1 laboratories and office spaces that flexibly adapt to the companies‘ needs. Additionally, IZB provides excellent infrastructure. At the Martinsried location, start-ups have access to modern conference rooms, a design hotel, the restaurants „The Bowl“ and „Seven and More“, as well as the Bio Kids kindergarten.

A strong network
A vital success factor for IZB start-ups is the close proximity of both locations to cutting-edge research. On the Weihenstephan Campus, you’ll find the TUM school of Life Sciences of the Technical University of Munich, as well as the University of Applied Sciences Weihenstephan-Triesdorf. Adjacent to the IZB on the Martinsried/Großhadern campus, you‘ll find, among others, two Max Planck Institutes, faculties, and facilities of LMU, as well as the University Hospital of Munich-Großhadern. IZB fosters this strong network with an array of event formats like the IZBrunch and the Munich Life Science Pitch Day at the G2B Faculty Club, establishing itself as a key meeting point in the industry.

Name: Complement Therapeutics
Description:
Complement Therapeutics GmbH (CTx) is a German-headquartered biotechnology company focused on the research and development of novel therapeutics for complement-mediated diseases. The Company is a spinout from the University of Manchester and is based on the pioneering research of its founders into novel targets within the complement cascade. 

Our lead investigational product (CTx001) is being evaluated as a potential gene therapy for GA, a leading cause of blindness. Additional programs will evaluate potential therapeutic opportunities in other complement-mediated conditions. 

The Company has subsidiaries in the UK (Complement Therapeutics Ltd) and in the USA (Complement Therapeutics Inc) as well as research laboratories in Stevenage, UK.

About Geographic Atrophy
Geographic Atrophy (GA) is a leading cause of blindness in the elderly and represents the advanced stage of dry age-related macular degeneration. It is characterised by the progressive degeneration of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium, and choriocapillaris, resulting in irreversible vision loss. GA affects over 5 million people globally and remains a significant unmet clinical need.

About resminostat 
Resminostat is an orally administered class I, IIb and IV histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor that potentially offers an approach to treating different kinds of cancer. Resminostat demonstrated that it is well tolerated and can inhibit tumor growth and proliferation, cause tumor regression, and strengthen the body’s immune response to cancer.  Resminostat is currently being investigated in a pivotal study in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) as maintenance treatment by 4SC in Europe and by Yakult Honsha in Japan. 

About cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) 
CTCL is a rare disease with approximately 5,000 patients being newly diagnosed in Europe each year. The disease arises from malignant transformation of T-cells, a specialized subgroup of immune cells, primarily affects the skin, but may ultimately involve lymph nodes, blood and visceral organs. 
Currently, CTCL is not curable and treatment options for advanced-stage CTCL are limited. Although patients respond to the available treatment options, the duration of response is often short-lived and declines as the severity of the disease increases. The key therapeutic challenge in advanced-stage CTCL is therefore to make remissions more durable by halting disease progression and improving patient’s quality of life. 
 
About the RESMAIN study – resminostat for maintenance treatment of CTCL 
The pivotal RESMAIN study is being conducted at more than 50 clinical centers in 11 European countries and Japan. It will include more than 190 patients who suffer from advanced-stage cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) that have achieved disease control with systemic therapy.

Name: R-Biopharm Group
Description:
R-Biopharm AG, located in Darmstadt, is one of Germany’s leading biotechnology companies. It considers itself as a pioneer for health and quality of life. Name: Institute of Technical Biocatalysis - TUHH
Description:
For as long as we can remember, our planet has generously given us everything we have needed and everything we have wanted. Yet our resources are limited. Our next steps must be chosen carefully.
It is our ambition to do our best and to provide long-term as well as more environmentally friendly solutions by utilizing processes from nature. We are working on projects in which new products are created from waste materials and design new biocatalytic technologies for a more sustainable future. 
Through real-time analytics, detailed process control is enabled, resulting in a more responsible management of our resources and minimization of waste streams. We are digitalizing these processes to better understand them and to establish smart processes. 
To invent new and innovative methods, teamwork and interdisciplinary collaboration are of utmost importance. We are globally networked. Additionally, we cherish close cooperation with partners from industry, as this allows our research results to be implemented on a large scale. 
At the same time, this enables our students and employees to get in contact with industrial research and development at an early stage in their career. 
Thanks to our interdisciplinary and intercultural collaborative environment,
we have even more opportunities to develop new ideas and to put our visions into practice. We do not just want to help our students become better scientists, but also give them the freedom they need to develop as individuals.
To empower the future generation with new, sustainable solutions, 
we invite children and youths to come and experience the world of science and technology at our institute. 
As part of our "Kinderforscher" program, we develop and offer experiment kits to elementary and secondary schools. With our "Nachwuchscampus" program, we are bringing together schools, universities, and industry. 
And thirdly, we reach out to you digitally, with our online site kniffelix.de.

Description:
Custom Single-Domain Antibody Discovery & Nanobody-Based Research Tools

NanoTag Biotechnologies specializes in single-domain antibodies (sdAbs), also known as nanobodies or VHHs. Established in 2015 in the vibrant scientific hub of Göttingen, Germany, our company leverages deep expertise in biochemistry and advanced imaging techniques to effectively support academic research and pharmaceutical development.

Name: spcfy.io
Description:
spcfy unlocks biodiversity data through predictive analytics, bridging science and impact.

Designed for researchers, laboratories, and environmental organizations, spcfy is a cloud-based platform that processes and interprets DNA-based biodiversity data such as eDNA, metabarcoding, and barcoding. By combining molecular biology, geospatial data, and machine learning, it transforms complex sequencing results into actionable ecological insights.

spcfy standardizes and integrates data from multiple sources, including genetic sequences, environmental metadata, and GIS-based habitat information, to generate harmonized biodiversity profiles and predictive ecosystem models. Users can explore community compositions, detect biodiversity patterns across land-use gradients, and forecast ecological shifts under different environmental or management scenarios.

The platform supports the entire workflow from Illumina raw FASTQ upload to data validation, quality control, and interactive result visualization. All computations are performed within secure AWS infrastructure, ensuring data ownership, privacy, and reproducibility. spcfy’s automated reporting makes it easy to integrate biodiversity insights into research, environmental monitoring, and sustainability decision-making.

Whether you are a lab offering sequencing services, a research institution exploring biodiversity dynamics, a company assessing ecological footprints, or an agency designing nature-based solutions, spcfy enables you to transform data into understanding and action.

Our mission is to make biodiversity monitoring available, affordable, and actionable because nature counts, and data should too.

Name: Sovicell
Description:
Sovicell develops and manufactures TRANSIL assay kits for preclinical ADME and DMPK research. Our mechanistic test systems quantify plasma protein binding, membrane binding, intracellular binding and drug distribution. They are designed for measurements where conventional methods are challenged by very low unbound fractions, poor solubility, nonspecific binding or complex binding behaviour.

A particular strength of the TRANSIL portfolio is the quantitative measurement of strongly and extremely strongly plasma protein-bound compounds. Specialized assays are available for unbound fractions far below 1%, including fu values of 0.01% or less, where conventional methods may be limited by analytical sensitivity, nonspecific binding or method-dependent artefacts.

TRANSIL assays support the characterization of small molecules, peptides, macrocycles, PROTACs and other emerging drug modalities. Core applications include:

• Plasma protein binding, including very low unbound fractions
• Albumin and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein binding
• Intracellular and tissue binding
• Brain distribution and intracellular drug bioavailability
• Microsomal and hepatocyte binding
• Membrane partitioning and permeability

TRANSIL assays combine controlled experimental systems with quantitative models. This allows researchers to derive biologically meaningful parameters, evaluate model fit and assess whether the assumptions underlying the measurement are supported by the experimental data.

Sovicell technologies have been used in pharmaceutical research for more than two decades and are supported by peer-reviewed publications and collaborations with leading industrial and academic research groups.

Name: CellDEG GmbH
Description:
CellDEG GmbH was founded 2016 and is a spin-off from the Institute of Biology at the Humboldt University of Berlin. Members of the former Cell Biology group headed by Prof. Dr. Rudolf Ehwald developed the High-Density Cultivation (HDC) process for optimal CO2 and light supply of cyanobacteria and microalgae. Compared to classical culture methods, the productivity of photoautotrophic microorganisms can thus be increased several folds.

The technology is based on highly efficient membrane-mediated CO2 transfer into turbulently moving cell suspensions. In combination with strong light and nutrient-enriched media, unprecedented volume- and area-based biomass productivities up to very high cell densities (≥ 30 g dw L-1) can be generated in this way. Features such as the avoidance of carbon and light limitation, disturbingly high oxygen concentrations, bubble flow-induced shear stress, negligible CO2 and water vapor losses to the atmosphere as well as the possibility of axenic cultivation make this system unique.

Based on this technology, CellDEG has developed parallel screening and analysis platforms as well as bioreactors for the production of axenic biomass at laboratory scale. All cultivators offered can be connected to a central control unit and enable a convenient and time-saving workflow. These highly innovative cultivation systems are marketed primarily to research institutions and biomass producers who want to grow cyanobacteria and microalgae quickly, in parallel and reliably. CellDEG aims to establish a standardized highly efficient technology for photoautotrophic cultures that allows reproducibility of experimental approaches across laboratories. The associated sensor technology and analytics, as well as the transfer of the technology to the pilot plant scale, are also key areas of focus.

Name: Modiblast
Description:
Modiblast Pharma is advancing into the clinical phase with a groundbreaking approach to Dendritic Cell Therapies for liquid cancers. The critical challenge in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) is the very high relapse rate after successful initial treatment.
Our therapy directly addresses this by reprogramming patients’ own leukemic blasts through immunomodulators into leukemia-specific dendritic cells (DCleu). These induced DCleu act as powerful antigen-presenting cells, activating both innate and adaptive immune responses to eliminate residual or recurring blasts and to establish long-lasting immune surveillance.
By this strategy, the patient’s immune system is directed to recognize the full, individual repertoire of leukemic antigens—without the need to pre-select molecular targets.
Compared to approaches like CAR-T, our strategy offers decisive advantages:
- No complex or costly ex vivo engineering
- No reliance on specialized GMP facilities
- Potential for a simple, self-administered drug to sustain remission or block disease progression
Beyond AML, this therapy also shows promise for myelodysplastic syndrome and other cancers, with the potential to normalize thrombocyte and neutrophil counts.

Description:
Just 10 years ago GPs experience and intuition was enough to determine the best antibiotic for patients. Since then however antibiotic resistance raised significantly. Same antibiotic can work differently for two patients suffering from the same disease. 

Countries like France, Denmark, Switzerland, and Germany already made the first move to decelerate this problem, as they established the law for mandatory testing before prescription of an antibiotic. 

As an ideology, this regulation is more than great, but it has one major problem. In order to work properly, it needs to be quick and cheap enough to be used in case of every patient regardless of their health condition.

We aim to design, prove and then mass-produce cheap and quick point-of-care tool that will help GPs select proper antibiotic for every patient. This will reduce the mortality caused by improper treatment of bacterial diseases. The precise selection of an antibiotic for infection treatment will also slow down the drug-resistance process.

We developed the testing machine that houses all necessary equipment to carry our test (including analytic algorithm) that will be sold one time to clinics and testing plates including our own recipe mixture of antibiotics, nutrition broth and enhancers that will be sold weekly to clinics based on their needs.

Our motivation is to develop the tool to resolve a worldwide issue. We hope to encourage governments to implement mandatory antibiotic selection testing by delivering a viable solution that allows such law without stretching healthcare budgets.

vasQlab - for safe drug testing.

vasQlab is an EXIST-founded KIT spin-off, taking our research to the market, because we believe in the impact it is going to have on pharmacological development, research without animals, safety in clinical trials and the successful release of new medications. 

With our vasQchip technology, we provide a platform that replicates organ-specific, human tissues in vitro. It allows the use of human cell material, high throughput testing, individual setting of parameters and continous oberservation. The center of these vasQchips is a curved porous microchannel presenting a microfludic blood vessel. This artificial blood vessel is surrounded by tissue-specific 3D cell cultures, where we currently focus on the blood brain barrier, liver, gut, skin and tumor models. Like that, our vasQchip allows for research on both substance or drug transport and performance, on the interplay between blood stream and tissue and also on the interaction between different tissues conntected by their vascularization.
